quest.title: All's Well That Ends Well
quest.description: You and Paimon patrolled the area near the abnormal ley line deposit for several days. It is time now, it seems, to report back to Adelinde.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: You're finally back.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: I didn't think you'd be gone for so long. Sorry if it was too much trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's okay. We did offer to help.

choices.text: Even if we hadn't gone to Falcon Coast...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So anyway, is Master Diluc back yet? We didn't see him at Falcon Coast.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Sorry, I'm not sure of Master's whereabouts either. But I did hear that he recently visited Angel's Share.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: After dealing with this kind of trouble, Master is always careful to tie up all loose ends. It's become something of a routine.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: He should be back very soon. You needn't worry. In the meantime, please make yourself comfortable in the Winery.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all that, we managed to completely miss him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh well. Let's just wait for him at the Winery this time.

choices.text: (At least we got to see the Diluc of the past.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Adelinde, how come you're always standing here at the door lately? Usually, you're busy indoors.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hopefully you haven't been standing there waiting for Master Diluc this whole time...? 'Cause that would be reeeally tiring!

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Oh, thanks for your concern. But I've actually been instructed by Master to meet with some special guests here.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Certain guests may need reminding to stay away for the time being.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Master hopes that under the present circumstances, these guests will keep an appropriate distance from the Winery, so as not to make a difficult situation even more complicated.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Well, Paimon didn't understand any of that, but... it sounds like a really important job.

choices.text: What is it that you need our help with?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: That's very kind of you indeed, but you've already helped Master Diluc out a great deal. You can let me take care of these time-consuming chores.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: There is one small thing you could do for me, though. Please take this letter and place it on the table to your right as you enter the door.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: There are a few archived letters on that table already. Just put this one at the very top of the pile.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this a letter for Master Diluc?

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Yes, it's from one of his informants. Only those in Master's inner circle are permitted to handle it or serve as custodian.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that means we're part of Diluc's inner circle!

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Of course. Master Diluc greatly values your friendship. Thanks again for the help.

choices.text: Maybe we could help meet those guests?
(It was worth it for that experience.)
We probably would have been fighting monsters somewhere else...

talks.objective: Enter the Winery and find Diluc's desk

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's sort Diluc's letters for him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, since he said he doesn't mind, why don't we read them as we go?

talks.objective: Enter the Winery and find Diluc's desk

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there are so many letters here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like Diluc read them just before he left. He must have been in a hurry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Adelinde asked us to put this one at the top of the pile, but how are we supposed to tell the order of the other ones?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we'll have to read them to get an idea of when they came in.

choices.text: We really shouldn't be reading other people's mail...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. In that case, let's just tidy them up a little.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: You're here? You move fast.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! There he is!

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: What are you agonizing over?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ms. Adelinde asked us to put these letters in a pile, and we can't tell which order they should go in...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it's your personal mail, so it'd be rude for us to read them without your permission.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: There's no need to be nervous.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: ...And I can see from the looks on your faces that they've grabbed your interest.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: These letters deal with events that are past and gone. I only held onto them in case any of the information they contain proves useful later down the line.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: I just dug them out to confirm a few details, I've been following some rather unique developments recently.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: You were involved in the events in question anyway. You can read them if you want to. It's not a bad thing to be curious.

choices.text: Are you in a hurry?
You seem to be in a huge rush...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that's a good point... Actually, you kinda smell like wild mountain fruit... Oh! Did you go to those mountains where the Valberries come from?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Very perceptive. Yes, I did make a trip to the Stormbearer Mountains.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: I'll fill you in later.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Diluc swiftly goes upstairs...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No fair! We still have some super important things to discuss with Diluc... not to mention a whole bunch of questions!

choices.text: Paimon, you need to calm down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Alright, let's just sort these letters for him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, since he said he doesn't mind, why don't we read them as we go?

choices.text: It's been a long time since Diluc's presence last overawed you, huh.
You don't look like you just got back from the city...
Do you still have other business to attend to?
Wait, let me think...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bad idea? Yeah, you're probably right... Okay, let's just tidy them up a little.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm all set.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then, let's put the letters in the right order.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If there's one thing we can take away from these, it's that Master Diluc has had a pretty difficult past...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not only was he misunderstood by the Knights of Favonius, but he's faced all kinds of other obstacles, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like it's tough being Captain Pyro.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Always fighting alone, because for one reason or another, it wasn't convenient for the people around him to help out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But Diluc seems to have found some peace since then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, he's got us now. We can give him all the help he could ever want!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh — out of friendship, of course! Definitely not just for the grape juice!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... what?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Is there a problem?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Master Diluc... you're wearing your old outfit again? And you've tied your hair back...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look so formal all of a sudden!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: "Old outfit"? You've seen it before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, it was by that ley line anomaly... That was your past self, right?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Huh. I'm surprised it made such an impression.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you mind telling us about it? What happened back then? Why were you fighting there?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The same reason as ever. Just stopping another Abyss Order plot.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: They launched an offensive on several fronts at once. Unfortunately for them, they were still no match for me.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: We were fighting in an area on Falcon Coast, and everything was recorded by the unusually active ley lines.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: They must have become unstable again recently, causing them to let out all kinds of information from that time. Hence why you saw what you saw.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why didn't you stay there to keep guard?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: For starters, you only need to deal with the monsters and the ley line deposit will stay dormant, as long as it isn't disturbed again.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: On the other hand, if I'd done nothing at all, the Knights of Favonius would have taken over straight away. Knowing how they work, they'd be sure to send a large contingent to guard the site.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wouldn't that have been a good thing?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Depends. Most of the knights are away on expeditions, so they don't have a lot of people to spare.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: If the ley line anomaly was just a diversion tactic, the Abyss Order could have been poised to attack somewhere else entirely, while the knights were scrambling to send what limited forces they have to Falcon Coast.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: But anyway, I have no interest in talking to the Knights of Favonius. I prefer to get to the bottom of things myself rather than waste time negotiating with them.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: And it was easy enough for me find out the Abyss Order's plans. Take a few Abyss Mages hostage, and they soon start talking.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: As for the Knights of Favonius, I've sent someone to enlist their cooperation where it's needed.

choices.text: So this is a joint initiative between you and the Knights.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: It's their job to handle situations like this. They ought to be present when things come to a head.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: I don't like working closely with the Knights of Favonius because of our differences in philosophy, but that doesn't mean we can't watch each others' backs when it counts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... seems like you have even more control over things now than you used to, Diluc.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: The best way to deal with any threat is to utilize all the force at your disposal.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Anyway, thank you for your help, Adelinde brought me up to speed with everything. In return, I have a gift for your trouble.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Grape juice?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The packaging is so fancy! It must be really expensive?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: This is my personal favorite grape juice, made of the highest-quality grapes. I happened to have an unopened batch, so I brought you a bottle to try.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: I didn't know you were such fans of grape juice. Next time you want some, don't bother waiting for the discount — just go down to the cellar and help yourselves.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: It's on the house.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo! Paimon's gonna tell everyone we meet that we're VIPs at Dawn Winery!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This one bottle must be worth at least... like, fifty thousand Mora? Hee-hee, and he gave it to us for free...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you, Master Diluc!

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Haha... If you're free tonight, you're welcome to stay for dinner. Adelinde is already making it.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: There are, however, a few things I need to take care of before dinnertime.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Things that involve fighting?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Yes. Passiveness is not my style.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Though I had my suspicions at the start, everything I've come across so far in my investigation suggests that the Abyss Order was not behind this.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Since this arose from natural causes, it's time to wrap things up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}... Um, so what should we do...?

choices.text: Well, in for one Mora, in for the lot...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, sure! After all, he did just give us this amazing grape juice...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, no... what was it... After all, "even when the odds of success are nine to one, you must never lower your guard."

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Well said.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: In that case, let's get going.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okie-Dokey, Captain Pyro! You can take it a little easier this time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, let's go! This is the final battle, then we can put all this trouble behind us!

choices.text: We help Diluc out.
It almost sounds like you're doing the Knights of Favonius a favor.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: There, it's done.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The ley line deposit will disappear before long.

choices.text: That battle went very smoothly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All thanks to the power of teamwork!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, even Captain Pyro needs his trusty sidekicks sometimes. It can't be Master Diluc saving the day by himself every single time. Many hands make light work!

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Sidekicks, hmm...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: It's been a long time since I last worked with others. It's not so bad.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: If the opportunity arises, let's team up again in the future.

choices.text: That battle was a lot of fun.

talks.objective: Go to the abnormal ley line deposit again

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Do you want to keep reading them? Or have you got the gist now, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's read one more letter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. Remember, we're trying to figure out when each letter was written.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Please make yourselves comfortable in the Winery.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: And thanks again for helping with the letter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon's not sure what this one's about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Shall we read another one, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Hello, Master Kae— Ahem, I mean Captain Kaeya.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: I don't believe we were expecting you. Has something urgent come up?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh, Adelinde, don't be such a stranger, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius have received word of another sighting of the Darknight Hero. Now, the witness wasn't able to see where the suspect was headed, however...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I just have a gut feeling that he's in the Dawn Winery area.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Really? What can I say, Captain Kaeya... You and the Darknight Hero have never been seen in the same place at the same time, and you often show up at the Dawn Winery — just like the Darknight Hero.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: So is it safe to say that... you are the Darknight Hero?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, now that you mention it, it makes sense. I almost can't believe it — I am the legendary Darknight Hero!

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Captain Kaeya, but the Dawn Winery is having a fire safety inspection today.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: You'll have to come back another day.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Seriously? Shouldn't you at least ask me to stay for dinner, as a courtesy?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Then again, I do have a pile of admin work waiting for me today...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: In that case, please pass a message on to Diluc for me. Tell him that the hazard zone has been established, the public shouldn't notice anything, and the enemy is unlikely to detect it right away.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Captain Kaeya, your words are as profound and enigmatic as ever. I'm just a maid, none of that means anything to me.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Master is currently out at a business meeting with his commercial partners. I don't know where they are exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: I will pass your message on to him word for word when he gets back, but I can't guarantee that the meaning behind the words will be fully conveyed.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh? But these are code words he grew up using. If he doesn't understand them... then perhaps it was a wasted childhood.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, is there anything new at the Winery? While I'm here, I'd like to pick up some choice wine to take home.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Captain Kaeya, you are too funny. You know we don't do retail.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Still, thank you so much for visiting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Dear Diluc,

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Welcome back to Mondstadt, Sir.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: It has been some time since the incident. We discovered that Eroch had betrayed us, and he has been punished severely.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I hope that this news will put your mind at ease.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: In other news, our people have discovered that the Abyss Order has stepped up its activities between Wolvendom and Stone Gate lately.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Also — a mysterious individual that people are calling the "Darknight Hero" has suddenly started showing up out of nowhere all around Mondstadt City. He typically acts in the dead of night, and his intentions are currently unclear.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Please stay safe, and notify the Knights as soon as possible should you see anything suspicious. We will send support immediately.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Whether you are presently in our ranks or not, all faithful knights will remember your contributions to the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: May you remain in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Neatly Written Letter

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: Dear Mr. Diluc,

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: It is my pleasure to investigate the ley lines alongside you.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: As you know, my focus is on alchemy, so my knowledge of the ley lines remains quite shallow, and I fear that I will only be able to share what little understanding I have.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: According to many pre-existing documents, the ley lines can be seen as a medium for storing information. Under certain circumstances, they can record activities that occur in the area around them.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: All this information goes through a recording and storage process. After a certain period of time, they may be released once again by the ley lines.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: If I may be so bold as to make a guess, there should be a method to activate the ley lines. Those who grasp such methods can control the times at which ley line information is recorded and released.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: Judging from the runic symbols and some other clues, I surmise that there are particular members of the Abyss Order who may have a very small chance of being able to achieve this.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: If you believe that this requires further investigation, these entities may serve as your point of entry.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: I wrote a paper a few years ago in which I covered my brief foray into questions concerning the flow of ley lines and other such topics. You will find a copy of this paper enclosed.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: I hope that it can help to clear up some of your doubts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Letter With Rough Handwriting

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Diluc,

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Jean wrote to me lately with shocking news. If I don't miss my guess, she wrote to you too. Her sentiments are those of the Knights as a whole.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Crepus was a good man, and I thought very well of him. It grieves me greatly to know that he met with such a fate.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: As for the defeat of the drake, the honors for that accomplishment should go to your father. I do not accept Eroch's theft of the credit for that deed, which was bought with your father's sacrifice.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Stolen credit will not be accepted within the Knights of Favonius under any circumstances. I will not permit it.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: I have already given Jean the authority to punish Eroch with all necessary severity. The Knights will inform you of the results.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: I've heard that you've been taking some time off outdoors and may not be easy to reach, so there is no guarantee that my letter will reach you. As such, I'll stop here for now.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: If it does reach you, then I wish you good health and safety in your travels. Contact us if you need anything.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: I hope that falcon of yours will help put this letter in your hands. I mean, I don't write in person very often, you know?

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: These may seem like pointless words to you right now, but remember: even the greatest of disasters must come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Mondstadt waits for your return, and if you're willing, the Knights will always welcome you. (If you're not, forget I said anything, yeah?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Tidily Written Letter

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: To the heir of the Ragnvindr Clan,

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: I apologize for sending this letter without notice. You may not remember me, but we've met a few times.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: We've met near the square, when I sat at the table adjacent to yours at the Good Hunter, and I've seen you in your tavern...

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: You were always busy with a great many things, especially back when you were much chattier than you are now. You spoke cheerfully and often with your brother and friends then.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: It's probably no surprise that you did not notice me then. But I've always had my eye on you, child.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: I recall with crystal clarity how my little Klee once made a complete mess of your vineyard while she was trying to catch Crystalflies there...

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: But you didn't get angry. In fact, you personally escorted Klee back and even gave her a few bottles of fresh grape juice.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Now I think that might jog your memory, yes?

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Klee recently told me that she "hasn't seen that strange man with the red hair in aaages," so I decided to look into it out of curiosity.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: My deepest condolences regarding your father.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: In many of the stories I've been told, you are the model knight: proud, driven, a knight of noble character and lineage.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: But I know that you're gentler than you appear. If you weren't, you wouldn't have treated Klee the way you did.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: And since you helped my child out, I hope you won't mind if I treat you as if you were my own.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Therefore, I sincerely hope that you will leave the dark place that you are presently in, and that you will not wallow in grief and remorse.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Partings are most painful things, but they also encourage us to grow. A bird that has lost the roof over its head will fly further than others of its kind.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Go out and see the world. That's the best course of action I can envision. Only by feeling, observing, and listening can your heart be healed.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Parents all wish that they can accompany their children forever, and the skies, seas, and stars bear witness to that oath.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Everything that was your father now finds new life with you. That which you will experience in this world may have been things that your father experienced once upon a time.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: I hope that the wind will bring you all manner of wondrous things in your journeys to come.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: In any case, keep your chin up, young child.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Letter With Clear Handwriting

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Master,

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Master Kaeya took leave and stayed at Dawn Winery for a few days.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: In a rare turn of events, he decided to stay in his original bedroom. He would pace about the grounds when idle, and even asked Adelinde to make him his favorite dishes.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Ah, it really does take me back.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: I shall be honest with you, but I was quite surprised to hear Master Kaeya say that he wanted to stay for a few days.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: We did not refuse him, however. We believe that even if you were here, you would not refuse him outright.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Dawn Winery has always been a more quiet location, perhaps because all who stay here are rather peaceable people.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: The house is made by those who live in it, and Master Kaeya's uncommon arrival did end up livening the place up significantly.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: I hope that you are doing well in your travels abroad. Everyone here at the winery misses you.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: May you remain safe and in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A New Letter

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: Dear Darknight Hero, the Knights of Favonius have stepped up the guard details throughout Mondstadt without making any major movements. The Abyss Order will not have noticed.

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: I am scouting around Dragonspine. The monsters here are scattered and separated. Clearly, they haven't been assembled by the Abyss Order.

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: There are no signs of enemy activity in the south of Mondstadt either.

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: If you can confirm that the other locations are also free of monsters, we will be able to conclude that the Abyss Order has nothing to do with the recent ley line disorder.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been fighting here for a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's starting to wonder if we should've left the ley line deposit alone... Maybe then, the monsters would have stopped coming...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, Paimon still doesn't have a clue what's going on here... Shall we just go ask Diluc?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, c'mon, let's get back to the Dawn Winery, {NICKNAME}.
